content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors proposed “DEEP DUPLEX LEARNING FOR WEAK SUPERVISION” in this paper. Both the supervision and counter-supervision signals are exploited for training for the implicitly and adaptively balance. A duplex representation composed of a superficial representation (SR) and a hypocritical representation (HR) is used in this paper. A general framework is proposed in this paper, but the authors try to cover too many situations in the framework. I think it may be better to focus on the details of one situation. Only two data sets are used and the experiment may be inadequate.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: Clear structure and necessary formulations.

Weaknesses: I think it may be better to focus on the details of only one situation, and give more experimental results.
1. A general framework is proposed in this paper, covering cover learning
with noisy labels, partial label learning, and semi-supervised learning. I think it may be better to focus on the details of one situation.
2. As to the supervision and counter-supervision signals, whether additional artificial work is needed or not?
3.Only two data sets (CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100) are used and the experiment may be inadequate.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper is well-written, a general framework is proposed in this paper, covering many aspects. Weak supervision is now a hot issue, authors have given some useful points. I think it may be better to focus on the details of only one situation, and give more experimental results. This work is reproducible.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes deep duplex learning, a paradigm for learning from noisy labels, partial labels, or pseudolabels. The authors evaluate DDL on standard benchmarks from noisy labels, partial labels, and pseudolabels.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
+ This framework may be helpful to organize research around noisy/partial/pseudolabels.
+ In some tasks, DDL seems to outperform baselines.

- The paper overclaims its results. In many tasks, results are within error bars of state-of-the-art results.
- Figure 1 seems almost intentionally misleading; there does not appear to be a consistent scale to the results.
- Limited methodological novelty; the paper mostly takes existing methods and puts it into the framework.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: The paper is not particularly clear. Some terms are used before they are defined.

Quality: There are many experiments, but the results are overclaimed. Multiple results in tables 1-4 are bolded but within error bars of the second best result.

Figure 1 is very misleading. There does not appear to be a consistent scale to the results.

Novelty: Limited novelty. This paper appears to largely take existing SoTA methods and run them, with limited changes.

Reproducibility: Seems fine.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall I think this paper is below the acceptance threshold. The technical contributions are limited, and the empirical results are not impressive (may be due to noise).

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper propose a new method, called deep duplex learning (DDL),  attempts to deal with noise label learning, partial label learning, and semi-supervised learning, from a unified perspective of supervision utilization. Through the modulation of supervision signal and counter-supervision signal, the model is capable of adaptively reducing the effect of false supervisions, so as to improve the learning from weak supervised information.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Through the modulation of supervision signal and counter-supervision signal to help improve model with weak supervised information is interesting, and expected to strengthen the robustness of model against various kinds of weak supervision information. However, there exist some concerns as follows:
- The formulation is not clear to me, and I hardly understand the rigorous principle of proposed method, and there exist many typos in the formulas. E.g., in Eq(2), $a(y)$ should be $a(x)$, $e^{w_a(y)y}$ should be $e^{w_{a(y)}\cdot y}$. $L(s,a)$ is not defined, and $s$ is ambiguous, since there already define $s(y,p)$.  Especically, Eq.(5) is vacuous, and it is hard to distinguish loss and counter-loss. 
- Eq.(4) is the key idea of this paper,  while I can not understand why such revision can deal with various kinds of weak supervision information. A straight or intuitive explanation for the motivation is necessary. 
- Eq.(7) seems to be heuristic, and can not directly capture the insights.
- The superficial representation (SR) and a hypocritical representation (HR) are vacuous. 
- The completed algorithm is missing, and the whole learning process is not clear to me. Especically, how to combine with existing algorithms?
-  The improvement for baselines is not remarkable, and there are only tiny accuracy improvements in most cases. I can not understand the function of the proposed method.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The idea is interesting, while the writting and formulation is not clear to me. The novelty is doubt, since Eq.(4), (7) seems to be heuristic for me. The underlying motivations and insights is not clear to me. The algorithm is missing, and readers hardly reproduce the results.
content.summary_of_the_review: The writting of this paper is poor, and some of the statements in the paper are ambiguous and the explanation on key details is not reasonable. The formulation is vacuous, and readers hardly capture the motivations and insights. The main contribution of the work is not justified. The algorithm is missing, and readers hardly reproduce the results.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposed a method for learning from **noisy, partial, and pseudo** labels based on loss function modification. The method was only evaluated empirically.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Considering different types of weak supervision in a unified framework is beneficial. This work attempted to do this. The left half of Figure 2 is nice.

However, it seems the author failed to achieve a unified framework as they claimed. The proposed method is still a plugin and needs to be combined with other methods specifically designed for a certain kind of supervision (DivideMix, AugDesc, PiCO, and CoMatch).

Besides, the author used many vague and far-fetched metaphors ("superficial representation", "hypocritical representation", "entangle with each other", "collaborate with each other", etc.) without giving a rigorous mathematical definition, which I believe are very harmful to the machine learning community. The only definition of "superficial/hypocritical representation" I can find is "we regard the original representation as the SR and simply add a fully connected layer to obtain the HR", which is quite arbitrary.

I could not fully understand why this method may work and the benefits of this method.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The writing is confusing, so I could not properly assess the quality and novelty of this work.

In addition to the metaphor issue, the explanations are not very understandable.
For example: 
- What is "enforcement of certain relations between image representations and class prototypes"?
- How is the prototype $\mathbf{p}_i$ obtained?
- Why is the "amending factor" calculated this way? Where is the "duplex similarity function" derived from?

I read Section 3 with many questions, and my questions were not resolved even after reading a few times.
content.summary_of_the_review: I could not properly assess this work's contribution due to its confusing writing style. The novelty seems marginal because adaptive supervision selection methods do exist, unlike what the author claimed. The proposed method serves as a plugin to a base method, and the improvement may not be statistically significant (The author did not report how different methods are compared). Therefore I cannot recommend acceptance of this paper to ICLR.

content.title: Deep Duplex Learning for Weak Supervision
content.TL;DR: We propose a deep duplex learning method for general weakly-supervised learning.
content.abstract: Weak supervision widely exists in practice and shows various forms such as noisy labels, partial labels, or pseudo labels. As a weak supervisor might provide false training signals, most existing works focus on correcting the supervisor or ignoring certain constraints. While they tackle each type separately, we propose a deep duplex learning (DDL) method to deal with all kinds of weak supervision from a unified perspective of supervision utilization. We exploit both the supervision and counter-supervision signals for training and allow the network to implicitly and adaptively balance the two signals. We describe each image using a duplex representation composed of a superficial representation (SR) and a hypocritical representation (HR). We then impose the supervision signal and counter-supervision signal on SR and HR, respectively. The SR and HR collaborate to interact with the weak supervisor to adaptively confine the effect of false supervisions on the network. Our DDL sets new state-of-the-arts for noisy label learning, partial label learning, and semi-supervised learning on standard benchmarks.
